clue.text: Thirty days, in short — one for each shrub

parts.note: June has thirty days, and JUN is its short form
one is the Roman numeral I
per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: A tip for remembering the months gets oddly tied to buying shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty days' recalls the rhyme 'Thirty days hath September', but here it is one particular thirty-day month, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The juniper is an evergreen bush whose berries flavour gin.

clue.text: Raise money in America

definitions.meaning: to ... something up is to lift it with a ...
... is American slang for money, as in 'he hasn't got ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Lifting with a jack is raising; in US slang jack also means cash.

clue.text: Magi changing direction initially, going north for vengeance

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top
the first letter is a compass point, west, which is swapped for another compass point, south

parts.note: the Magi are the Three Wise Men of the Nativity story

explanation.surface: The Magi turn round and head north, seeking revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening W (west) for S (south) gives SISEMEN; 'going north' then reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, and the word now means retributive justice.

clue.text: Deposit put on a jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: to deposit a car is to park it

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a deposit and puts on a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof coat for cold weather is a kind of jacket.

clue.text: Game's course interrupted by replayed point

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the course is broken into, with the other piece placed inside it

parts.note: a route is a course to follow
in tennis a let is a point that has to be played again

explanation.surface: A tennis game's progress is held up by a point that must be replayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' signals a container. In tennis a let is called when a serve clips the net, so the point is played again.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Henry and I save swimmer in Atlantic

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
save means except, as does but: 'all but one'

explanation.surface: Henry and the speaker rescue someone swimming in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb about rescue; it is the preposition meaning 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish found in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Concealing punishment

definitions.meaning: keeping out of sight, the present participle of hide
a beating, as in 'he got a good thrashing'

explanation.definitionFit: Hiding something is concealing it; a hiding is also a sound thrashing.

clue.text: Pass laws on -one's passed on

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
one is I, and the 's adds S
someone who has passed on (died) is the late so-and-so

explanation.surface: Someone passes laws, and a person's death is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG for 'on' is cricket: the leg side, or on side, is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or enact laws is what a parliament does when it passes them.

clue.text: Traitor who lived in a borough?

definitions.meaning: Guy ..., one of the Cambridge spies who passed secrets to the Soviet Union
a citizen or freeman of a borough, the question mark marking a playful reading

explanation.definitionFit: Guy Burgess was a notorious British traitor; a burgess was historically an inhabitant of a borough.

clue.text: Wet tar at sea has absorbed study of how to avoid drowning

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the other piece, holding it inside
being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Tar soaks up a guide to keeping afloat at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' signals the anagram and 'has absorbed' the container. The definition is 'how to avoid drowning', with 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading water keeps a swimmer upright and afloat in one place.

clue.text: Be persuaded to wake up

definitions.meaning: to change one's mind and agree, as in 'she'll accept it eventually'

explanation.definitionFit: Coming round means being won over to a view, or regaining consciousness.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Cheddar in Somerset is famous for its limestone ravine; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to overeat; Cheddar Gorge is a ravine in Somerset, England, which gave the cheese its name.

clue.text: He has asked one mistreated to show disapproval

indicators.note: something mistreated is handled badly, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A man has asked someone who was treated badly to express disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the head from side to side is a gesture signalling no or disapproval.

clue.text: With a double, South maybe could get this

definitions.text: With a double, South maybe could get this

parts.words: With a double, South maybe could get this
parts.note: read as tennis, one more double fault could give the opponent the deciding point; at bridge, South is a player whose doubled contract may score top marks

explanation.definitionFit: The point that would decide a match, and also a style of bridge scoring.

clue.text: The ultimate in elegance and taste he contrived

definitions.text: The ultimate in elegance and taste he contrived

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are reordered
the very last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A man has devised the last word in elegance and good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ultimate in' takes the final E of elegance; with TASTE and HE, 'contrived' rearranges the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to beauty and refinement aims for exquisite style and taste.

clue.text: It heralds change in her garb

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seasonal change is signalled by what a woman wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or herald announces something coming, as the cuckoo announces spring.

clue.text: Rejected an application with a feeling of disgust

indicators.note: rejected, as in turned back, means the short word is read backwards

parts.note: use means application, as in putting a tool to use

explanation.surface: An application form is turned down with a sense of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns only 'an' into NA; 'with' links it to USE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness in the stomach, and by extension strong loathing.

clue.text: In display of affection, the French will appear casual

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, stated at the head of the clue

parts.note: a caress is a loving stroke
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people seem relaxed when showing affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' is the container signal; 'will appear' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless or offhand attitude is casual, without proper attention.

clue.text: Hawk eating the lady's fruit

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other piece in, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to hawk goods is to cry them in the street
her means belonging to the lady

explanation.surface: A bird of prey devours a woman's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb: street sellers hawk or cry their wares.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round stone fruit, red or black, from a tree of the plum family.

clue.text: I'm an example of this — I lose in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they lose, and are in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not the container signal it looks like: I LOSE IN has seven letters. 'I'm' shortens 'I am' by dropping a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving out a sound or syllable in speech is what turns 'I am' into a contraction.

clue.text: European iron put back into magnificent house

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a palace is a splendid residence

indicators.note: put back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Iron fittings are returned to a stately home in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the iron symbol and 'into' places it inside the house. In old Westerns the word was used for white settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Westerns a white person, especially of European descent, was called this by Native Americans.

clue.text: Week in a hospital room is difficult to deal with

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ward is a room for patients in a hospital

explanation.surface: Spending a week on a hospital ward is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky or clumsy situation or person is one that is hard to manage.

clue.text: Current classmates

definitions.meaning: a flow of water, as in a river
in British schools pupils of similar ability are grouped into the same set

explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flowing current, and in British schools it is a group of pupils taught together by ability.

clue.text: Pest that makes head's supporter uncomfortable

definitions.meaning: literally an ache in the part of the body that holds up the head

explanation.definitionFit: An irritating person is called this idiom, which literally names a sore neck.

clue.text: To catch pike, initially, in river, line is cast out

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An angler casts out a line to catch pike on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside EXE, giving EXPE, then L. 'To catch' and 'is' are link words dressing the fishing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or eject someone, such as from a school.

clue.text: Force-feed, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so what counts is how it sounds

parts.note: to dine is to eat or feed

explanation.surface: Someone is force-fed, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force-feed' reads as one word, but splits into the definition and the word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The dyne is the old unit of force in the centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: In Arctic, in Greenland, it's a problem for pilots

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Flying in the Arctic around Greenland is tricky for aviators.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'In' is the signal; the letters run from the end of Arctic, through 'in', into Greenland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice building up on an aircraft's wings is a hazard for those flying it.

clue.text: As a warning to others, Mary, 23, is replaced

indicators.note: replaced in the sense of put back in a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: 23 refers to the answer to clue 23, which means to cast out

explanation.surface: Mary is sacked to deter others.
explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to the answer to 23 Down, whose five letters join MARY's four for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishment meant to deter others is called exemplary, setting an example.

clue.text: Puzzle that's difficult in the extreme with a missing clue

indicators.note: the extreme of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken
missing means a letter is absent from the word for the clue type

parts.note: an anagram is a type of crossword clue
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A puzzle is extremely difficult because a clue is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the extreme' picks the final letter of difficult; 'missing' removes one A from the clue type.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese dissection puzzle of seven shapes arranged into figures.

clue.text: Painting initially in second place is a daub

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: a lodge is a dwelling, a place to live

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An artist's work that came second is dismissed as a mere smudge.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside S LODGE, straight after the S. 'second place' looks like a ranking but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a messy blot or smear of paint or ink.
